mainTopic: Cooking-related rules on שבת: returning a pot to the כירה, the תנור and כופח, and heating with indirect heat (an egg by the urn, the טבריה water pipe)
overview: The amud first finishes the point that בית הלל allow returning a pot to the כירה even on שבת. It supports this with רבי חייא רבה's silence when a kettle was returned in front of him. It then asks whether this applies only while the pot is still in hand or even after it was set on the ground. רבי תדאי, רבי יוחנן, and two reports of רבי אלעזר disagree, and חזקיה in the name of אביי adds the factor of intention (דעתו להחזיר) in two versions. Questions about a stick, a bed, and pouring into another urn end in תיקו. A new משנה then contrasts the תנור with the כופח. רב יוסף and אביי argue over whether leaning a pot against a תנור is allowed, and a ברייתא backs אביי. The גמרא explains that a כופח holds an in-between amount of heat and has room for only one pot. A third משנה forbids cooking an egg with indirect heat and tells the story of the טבריה water pipe. The amud ends with רב יוסף ruling that roasting the egg makes one liable for a חטאת, and a proof that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Returning the pot is allowed even on שבת
steps.stepSummary: This line finishes the previous discussion. It concludes that בית הלל's 'אף מחזירין' (one may even return) applies even on שבת itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...one may even return it, even on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the conclusion it reached on the previous amud: בית הלל allow returning the pot to the stove even on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was whether בית הלל permit returning a pot only on ערב שבת or also on שבת itself. The answer is that it is allowed even on שבת. The rest of this passage builds on this conclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: We return (the pot to the stove)
A small stove with room for two pots

phrases.english: one may (even) return it, even on Shabbat.
phrases.notes: End of a sentence that started on the previous section of the daf.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to בית הלל, a pot may be returned to the stove even on שבת.

steps.title: רבי אושעיא holds the same view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that רבי אושעיא also understands 'אף מחזירין' to apply even on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אושעיא also holds that 'one may even return' means even on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names another אמורא who agrees with the conclusion. This sets up the proof story in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line only makes the claim. The evidence that רבי אושעיא holds this way comes next, in the story he tells.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Oshaya also holds
'one may even return' — even on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a supporting authority for the conclusion of Step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אושעיא permits returning a pot to the stove on שבת.

steps.title: The story of the kettle before רבי חייא
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא tells how his group returned a kettle of hot water to the stove in front of רבי חייא רבה, and רבי חייא said nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי אושעיא said: Once we were standing before רבי חייא רבה. We brought up a kettle of hot water for him from the lower floor to the upper floor, poured him a cup, and put the kettle back in its place. He did not say anything to us.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the proof for Step 2. It is a story of something done on שבת in front of a great teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key detail is that they returned the kettle to its place on the fire on שבת. רבי חייא רבה stayed silent. A great teacher would have protested if this were forbidden, so his silence shows it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A floor or story of a building
He said nothing to us (silent approval)

phrases.english: As Rabbi Oshaya said:
Once we were standing
before (lit. above) Rabbi Chiya the Great
and we brought up to him a kettle of hot water
from the lower floor to the upper floor,
and we poured him the cup,
and we returned it to its place,
and he did not say anything to us.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא: פַּעַם אַחַת הַיְינוּ עוֹמְדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the evidence for the claim in Step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That returning a pot to the stove on שבת is permitted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A story of something done in practice: רבי חייא רבה stayed silent when the kettle was returned on שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל's 'אף מחזירין' applies even on שבת, backed up by רבי חייא's silent approval.

steps.title: רבי תדאי: only while still in his hand
steps.stepSummary: רבי תדאי limits the permission: you may return the pot only if it is still in your hand. Once you put it down on the ground, you may not return it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זריקא said in the name of רבי אבא, who said in the name of רבי תדאי: They only taught this when the pots are still in his hand. But if he put them down on the ground, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins: under what conditions may you return the pot? רבי תדאי gives a strict limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Returning is allowed only while the pot is still in your hand. Putting it down on the ground shows that you were done with the stove. After that, putting it back looks like setting it on the fire fresh on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught (this rule) in the case of...
They are still in his hand

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זְרִיקָא אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא
phrases.english: Rabbi Zerika said that Rabbi Abba said
that Rabbi Tadai said:
They only taught this when they are still in his hand,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הִנִּיחָן עַל גַּבֵּי קַרְקַע — אָסוּר.
phrases.english: but if he placed them on the ground — it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זְרִיקָא אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי תַּדַּאי: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the permission established in Steps 1-3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Returning is allowed only while the pot is in hand. Once it is set on the ground, returning is forbidden.

steps.title: רבי אמי: רבי תדאי's view was his own
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי dismisses רבי תדאי's restriction as a personal opinion, not the accepted הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: What רבי תדאי did, he did on his own.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי rejects רבי תדאי's limit. This also sets up the correct teaching he gives next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לגרמיה הוא דעבד' means רבי תדאי was speaking for himself and not passing on what he was taught. So his restriction is not binding.

keyTerms.meaning: He did it on his own (a personal view, not the accepted teaching)

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
What Rabbi Tadai did —
he did on his own.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: רַבִּי תַּדַּאי דַּעֲבַד לְגַרְמֵיהּ הוּא דַּעֲבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the restriction stated in Step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי תדאי's whole restriction ('only while in hand').
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It is his own personal opinion and not the received teaching.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: even after setting it on the ground
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי gives the correct teaching in the name of רבי יוחנן: even if the pot was put on the ground, you may return it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what רבי חייא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Even if he placed it on the ground, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting רבי תדאי, רבי אמי gives the opposite, lenient ruling from רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אלא הכי' replaces the rejected view with the authoritative one. Putting the pot down on the ground does not cancel the right to return it.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, this is how (it was said)

phrases.english: Rather, this is what Rabbi Chiya said
in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ הַנִּיחָה עַל גַּבֵּי קַרְקַע — מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: Even if he placed it on the ground — it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected restriction with a lenient ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Returning is permitted even after the pot was set on the ground.

steps.title: רב דימי and רב שמואל בר יהודה disagree
steps.stepSummary: Two אמוראים, both quoting רבי אלעזר, disagree on the same question. One says only while in hand; the other says even after it was set on the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי and רב שמואל בר יהודה disagree about this, and both say their view in the name of רבי אלעזר. One said: while they are still in his hand, it is permitted; on the ground, it is forbidden. The other said: even if he placed them on the ground, it is also permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the same disagreement (in hand vs. on the ground) also appears in the name of רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two positions match רבי תדאי (strict) and רבי יוחנן (lenient). The new point is that this is a real, recorded מחלוקת, with two different reports of what רבי אלעזר held.

phrases.english: Rav Dimi disagrees about this
with Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda,
and both say it in the name of Rabbi Elazar.
One said: while they are still in his hand — permitted,
on the ground — forbidden.
And one said:

phrases.aramaic: הִנִּיחָן עַל גַּבֵּי קַרְקַע נָמֵי מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: if he placed them on the ground, it is also permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַב דִּימִי וְרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the same two positions from Steps 4 and 6 in a second tradition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מחלוקת: strict (only while in hand) vs. lenient (even after setting it on the ground).

steps.title: חזקיה (version 1): intention matters even while in hand
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה quotes אביי: even while the pot is in hand, returning is allowed only if he planned all along to return it. It follows that once it is on the ground, returning is forbidden even with that plan.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said in the name of אביי: What you said, that while they are in his hand it is permitted, applies only when his intention is to return it. But if his intention is not to return it, it is forbidden. By inference: on the ground, even if his intention is to return it, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה adds a new factor, the person's intention (דעתו להחזיר), to the strict opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, intention is a further requirement on top of holding the pot. Holding it without the intent to return is forbidden. The inference (מכלל) shows that the ground is worse: setting it down forbids returning no matter what he intended.

keyTerms.meaning: His intention is to return it

steps.confusionAlert: 'דעתו להחזיר' refers to his intention at the time he took the pot off the fire. It does not mean a new decision he made later.

phrases.english: Chizkiya said in the name of Abaye:
That which you said, while they are still in his hand — permitted,
we said this only when his intention is to return it,
but if his intention is not to return it — forbidden.
By inference, that on the ground

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁדַּעְתּוֹ לְהַחֲזִיר — אָסוּר.
phrases.english: even though his intention is to return it — forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר חִזְקִיָּה מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּאַבָּיֵי: הָא דְּאָמְרַתְּ עוֹדָן בְּיָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies the strict opinion in Step 7 by adding intention as a requirement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In hand: permitted only with intent to return. On the ground: forbidden regardless of intent.

steps.title: חזקיה (version 2): intention can save even the ground case
steps.stepSummary: A second version of חזקיה's statement: setting it on the ground forbids returning only when he did not plan to return it. With that plan, it is permitted. It follows that while it is in hand, returning is always allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: חזקיה said in the name of אביי: What you said, that on the ground it is forbidden, applies only when his intention is not to return it. But if his intention is to return it, it is permitted. By inference: while it is still in his hand, even if his intention is not to return it, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, more lenient report of חזקיה's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here intention is used to make things easier, not stricter. The ground case is allowed if he meant to return the pot. The in-hand case is allowed no matter what he intended. This is the exact opposite of version 1.
steps.whatToRemember: Version 1: intention is an extra requirement even in hand, and the ground is always forbidden. Version 2: intention can permit even the ground case, and in hand is always permitted.

phrases.english: Some say:
Chizkiya said in the name of Abaye:

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּאָמְרַתְּ עַל גַּבֵּי קַרְקַע — אָסוּר,
phrases.english: That which you said, on the ground — forbidden,

phrases.aramaic: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין דַּעְתּוֹ לְהַחֲזִיר,
phrases.english: we said this only when his intention is not to return it,
but if his intention is to return it — permitted.
By inference, that while they are still in his hand,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין דַּעְתּוֹ לְהַחֲזִיר — מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: even though his intention is not to return it — permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי, אָמַר חִזְקִיָּה מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּאַבָּיֵי: הָא דְּאָמְרַתְּ עַל גַּבֵּי קַרְקַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternate version of Step 8, reaching a more lenient result.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the ground: permitted with intent to return. In hand: permitted even without that intent.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה asks about a stick or a bed
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks about in-between cases: the pot was hung on a stick, or set on a bed. Is that like holding it in hand, or like putting it on the ground?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked: If he hung them on a stick, what is the law? If he placed them on a bed, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises cases that fall between 'in hand' and 'on the ground'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A stick and a bed are not the ground, but they are also not in his hand. The question is which category these middle cases belong to.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked:
If he hung them on a stick, what is the law?
If he placed them on a bed, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: תְּלָאָן בְּמַקֵּל מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the in-hand vs. on-the-ground line with in-between cases.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether hanging the pot on a stick or setting it on a bed counts as in hand or as on the ground.

steps.title: רב אשי asks about pouring into another urn
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks: if he poured the contents from one urn into another, may the second urn be put back on the fire?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי asked: If he transferred them from one urn to another urn, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A second question follows: what if the contents were moved into a different container?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The permission was for putting back the same pot. Moving the food into a new urn might make this a fresh placing on the fire and not a return.

keyTerms.meaning: An urn or kettle for heating water

phrases.english: Rav Ashi asked:
If he transferred them from one urn to another urn, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב אָשֵׁי: פִּינָּן מִמֵּיחַם לִמְיַחֵם מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another question about the edges of the rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether moving the food into a new container still counts as returning it.

steps.title: The questions remain unresolved
steps.stepSummary: All of these questions are left unresolved: תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand (unresolved).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the questions without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'תיקו' means no source settled the questions of רבי ירמיה and רב אשי. Later פוסקים have to decide how to rule when the question is left open.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: Holding the pot vs. setting it on the ground is debated, and intention plays a role. The in-between cases (stick, bed, another urn) were never resolved.

phrases.english: Let it stand (unresolved).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the questions of Steps 10 and 11 without answering them.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The questions about the stick, the bed, and transferring to another urn remain open (תיקו).

steps.title: משנה: an oven is forbidden, and a כופח depends on its fuel
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a תנור lit even with straw may not have a pot put inside it or on top of it. A כופח lit with straw is like a כירה, and lit with גפת or wood it is like a תנור.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: An oven that was heated with straw or stubble: one may not put a pot inside it or on top of it. A כופח heated with straw or stubble is like a stove. If it was heated with olive waste or wood, it is like an oven.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It moves from the כירה (stove) to two other heating devices, the תנור and the כופח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תנור holds heat very strongly, so even a weak fuel like straw makes it forbidden. A כופח is in-between, so its status depends on the fuel. Weak fuel makes it like a כירה, and strong fuel makes it like a תנור.

keyTerms.meaning: Oven; narrow at the top and holds heat strongly
A smaller cooking device with room for one pot
Olive or sesame waste left after pressing (a strong fuel)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the כופח with the כירה. A כופח only takes on the כירה's rules when it is lit with straw. It is its own type of device.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
An oven that they heated with straw or stubble

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִתֵּן בֵּין מִתּוֹכוֹ בֵּין מֵעַל גַּבָּיו.
phrases.english: one may not place a pot either inside it or on top of it.
A kupach that they heated with straw or stubble —
it is like a stove;
with olive waste or wood — it is like an oven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the תיקו that ended the previous discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תנור is forbidden inside and on top, even if lit with straw. A כופח is like a כירה with straw and like a תנור with גפת or wood.

steps.title: רב יוסף: only inside and on top are forbidden; leaning is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף reads the משנה literally: 'inside' and 'on top' are forbidden, but leaning a pot against the oven is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: About 'an oven that they heated': רב יוסף thought that 'inside' means really inside and 'on top' means really on top. But leaning a pot against it is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts on the משנה. רב יוסף proposes that the oven prohibition covers only putting the pot inside or on top.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה names only two forbidden placements. רב יוסף concludes that a third placement, leaning the pot against the outside wall, is allowed. This is the claim אביי will now attack.

keyTerms.meaning: He thought to say (often a view that gets challenged)
To lean a pot against the outside

phrases.english: GEMARA: 'An oven that they heated':
Rav Yosef thought to say
'inside it' means literally inside it,
'on top of it' means literally on top of it,
but to lean a pot against it is fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Interprets the wording of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With a תנור, only inside and on top are forbidden. Leaning a pot against it is permitted.

steps.title: אביי quotes the משנה and draws an inference
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes the כופח clause and infers that when a כופח is like a כירה, something is permitted that is forbidden when it is like a תנור.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected: 'A כופח heated with straw or stubble is like a stove. With olive waste or wood it is like an oven,' and forbidden. This implies that when it is like a stove, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins his challenge to רב יוסף. Here he only sets it up: he quotes the משנה and draws an inference from it. The next step finishes the attack.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה contrasts 'like a כירה' (permitted) with 'like a תנור' (forbidden). אביי will now ask what action the משנה is talking about, because that will show what is forbidden by a תנור.

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:

phrases.aramaic: כּוּפָּח שֶׁהִסִּיקוּהוּ בְּקַשׁ וּבִגְבָבָא הֲרֵי הוּא כְּכִירַיִים,
phrases.english: 'A kupach heated with straw or stubble is like a stove;

phrases.aramaic: בְּגֶפֶת וּבְעֵצִים הֲרֵי הוּא כְּתַנּוּר, וְאָסוּר.
phrases.english: with olive waste or wood it is like an oven,' and forbidden.
This implies: when it is like a stove — permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a challenge against רב יוסף's leniency.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that leaning a pot against a תנור is permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: the משנה contrasts a permitted 'כירה' status with a forbidden 'תנור' status. Identifying the action involved will reveal what is forbidden by a תנור.

steps.title: אביי proves the משנה must be about leaning
steps.stepSummary: Placing a pot on top cannot be the case, because on an uncleared כירה even that is forbidden. So the משנה must be about leaning, and it calls that forbidden for a תנור, against רב יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with? If you say putting it on top, then in what situation? If the coals were not swept or covered: on a stove that is not swept or covered, is putting a pot on top permitted? Rather, it must be about leaning. And the משנה teaches that it is like an oven and forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his challenge by eliminating the other options. Only 'leaning' fits the משנה, and the משנה forbids that with a תנור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An uncleared כירה is forbidden even on top. So the 'permitted like a כירה' case cannot be about placing a pot on top of an uncleared device. The only option left is leaning, and then 'like a תנור, forbidden' means leaning against a תנור is forbidden. That contradicts רב יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: With what case are we dealing?
Coals swept out, or covered with ashes
Rather, is it not that...? (forces the remaining option)

phrases.english: With what case are we dealing?
If you say on top of it, then in what situation?
If you say when it is not swept or covered with ashes,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כִּירָה כִּי אֵינָהּ גְּרוּפָה וּקְטוּמָה,
phrases.english: but a stove that is not swept or covered with ashes —
is putting a pot on top of it permitted?
Rather, is it not about leaning,
and it teaches: 'it is like an oven,' and forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's leniency about leaning a pot against a תנור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Process of elimination: the 'on top' reading fails for an uncleared device. The משנה must therefore be about leaning, and it forbids leaning with a תנור.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה: the case is a swept and covered device
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה says the משנה is about a device whose coals were swept or covered. A כירה like that is permitted on top, but a תנור is forbidden on top even then. So the משנה is about placing on top, not leaning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: Here we are dealing with a כופח that was swept and covered, and an oven that was swept and covered. 'It is like an oven' means that even though it was swept and covered, putting a pot on top is forbidden. If it were like a stove, then once swept and covered it would be fine.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה defends רב יוסף. He shows that the משנה can be about placing a pot on top after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי rejected the 'on top' reading only for an uncleared device. If the device was swept or covered, a כירה is permitted on top, while a תנור stays forbidden because it holds so much heat. The משנה then says nothing about leaning, and רב יוסף's leniency stands.

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
Here we are dealing with a kupach that is swept and covered,
and an oven that is swept and covered.
'It is like an oven' means:
that even though it is swept and covered,
putting a pot on top of it is forbidden;
for if it were like a stove, when swept and covered
it would be fine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: הָכָא בְּכוּפָּח גָּרוּף וְקָטוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge on behalf of רב יוסף.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא): the device is swept and covered
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה had to be about leaning, since 'on top' only works for an uncleared device.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about placing on top of a swept and covered device. A תנור is still forbidden then, and a כירה is permitted. Leaning is not discussed.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports אביי: leaning against an oven is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explicitly says one may not lean a pot against a תנור, even one lit with straw. A כופח with straw allows leaning but not placing on top, and with גפת or wood even leaning is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught in line with אביי: An oven heated with straw or stubble: one may not lean a pot against it. Needless to say one may not put it on top, needless to say not inside, and needless to say not when it was heated with olive waste or wood. A כופח heated with straw or stubble: one may lean a pot against it but may not put it on top. If heated with olive waste or wood, one may not lean a pot against it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that directly supports אביי's view against רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא explicitly forbids leaning a pot against a תנור, which is exactly what רב יוסף had permitted. It also builds up step by step: if leaning is forbidden, then on top and inside are certainly forbidden. For a כופח it lays out a middle ruling that depends on the fuel.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught supporting him
One may not lean a pot against it

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows the ברייתא and אביי. With a תנור, even leaning a pot against it is forbidden. With a כופח lit with straw, leaning is allowed but placing on top is not.

phrases.english: A baraita was taught in line with Abaye:
An oven that they heated with straw or stubble —
one may not lean a pot against it,
and needless to say not on top of it,
and needless to say not inside it,
and needless to say not when heated with olive waste or wood.
A kupach that they heated with straw or stubble —

phrases.aramaic: סוֹמְכִין לוֹ, וְאֵין נוֹתְנִין עַל גַּבָּיו.
phrases.english: one may lean a pot against it, but may not put one on top of it.
If heated with olive waste or wood, one may not lean a pot against it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב אדא's defense of רב יוסף, the גמרא brings an explicit source backing אביי.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's position that leaning a pot against a תנור is forbidden
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating 'תנור... אין סומכין לו'

steps.title: רב אחא asks: is a כופח like a stove or like an oven?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא asks רב אשי why the fuel matters. If a כופח is like a כירה, even wood should be fine. If it is like a תנור, even straw should be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא said to רב אשי: What is this כופח like? If it is like a stove, then even with olive waste or wood it should be permitted! If it is like an oven, then even with straw or stubble it should not be permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: A new question is raised about the כופח rule itself. Why does a כופח change its status depending on the fuel?
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the כירה and the תנור, the device's own type decides the rule. For the כירה, the fuel matters only for whether it must be cleared. For the תנור, even straw is forbidden. So it seems strange that a כופח switches categories based on fuel, and רב אחא wants to know what a כופח really is.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it like? How do we picture it?
If... and if... (setting up a dilemma)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rava said to Rav Ashi:
This kupach, what is it like?
If it is like a stove,
then even with olive waste or wood it should also be permitted!
If it is like an oven,
then even with straw or stubble it should also not be permitted!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: הַאי כּוּפָּח הֵיכִי דָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the logic behind the כופח rule laid out in the משנה and the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What category a כופח belongs to, and why its fuel changes its status.

steps.title: רב אשי: a כופח's heat is in-between
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that a כופח holds more heat than a כירה but less than a תנור. So weak fuel puts it with the כירה, and strong fuel puts it with the תנור.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Its heat is greater than a stove's, and its heat is less than an oven's.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question. A כופח is a middle case in how much heat it holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because a כופח is between the two, the fuel tips the balance. Straw leaves it near a כירה. Wood or גפת brings it up to the level of a תנור.
steps.whatToRemember: A כופח has a middle status. It holds more heat than a כירה and less than a תנור, so the fuel decides which one it follows.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Its heat is greater than a stove's
and its heat is less than an oven's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחא's question directly.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A כופח holds a middle amount of heat, so its fuel determines whether it follows the כירה or the תנור.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A כופח is an in-between device: like a כירה with weak fuel and like a תנור with strong fuel.

steps.title: What exactly is a כופח and what is a כירה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a כופח and a כירה are built and how they differ.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does a כופח look like, and what does a כירה look like?
steps.whatsHappening: The previous steps kept comparing a כופח to a כירה, so now the גמרא asks for a clear definition of each one. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 said a כופח holds more heat than a כירה. It never said what a כופח physically is, so the גמרא now asks for the physical difference.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it like? What are the circumstances?

phrases.english: What is a kupach like?
What is a kirah like?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining that the two devices hold different amounts of heat, the גמרא asks what each one physically is.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The physical shape that tells a כופח apart from a כירה.

steps.title: One pot space versus two pot spaces
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא explains that a כופח has room for one pot and a כירה has room for two.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: A כופח is a place for setting one pot. A כירה is a place for setting two pots.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר חנינא answers the question. A כופח has a spot for one pot, and a כירה has spots for two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is size. A כירה is like a double כופח, with two openings where pots sit over the fire. Because a כופח is smaller and tighter, it fits with רב אשי's point that it holds heat differently.

keyTerms.meaning: Setting a pot on the fire

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina said:
A kupach is a place for setting one pot.
A kirah is a place for setting two pots.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the definition question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A כופח has space for one pot, and a כירה has space for two pots.

steps.title: Proof from a broken stove in the laws of purity
steps.stepSummary: אביי, or some say רבי ירמיה, proves the definition from a משנה about a כירה or כופח that was split in half.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said, and some say רבי ירמיה said: We also learned this in a משנה. A כירה that was split along its length is pure. If it was split along its width, it is impure. A כופח, whether split along its length or along its width, is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a משנה from the laws of טומאה that supports רבי יוסי בר חנינא. The way a split stove's purity works only makes sense if a כירה has two pot spaces and a כופח has one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A broken vessel that cannot be used becomes טהור. If a two-pot כירה is split across its width, between the two pot spaces, each half still has a full pot space and can still be used, so it stays טמא. A one-pot כופח split in any direction leaves no full pot space, so it is always טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: We also learned this, a formula for bringing support from a source
Along its length / along its width

steps.confusionAlert: This משנה is about טומאה, not שבת. It is brought here only because it shows the physical shape of each device.

phrases.english: Abaye said, and some say Rabbi Yirmeya:
We too have also learned this:
A kirah that was split lengthwise is pure.
phrases.notes: Each half has only half of each pot space, so the stove is broken and unusable.

phrases.english: Widthwise, it is impure.
phrases.notes: Each half keeps one full pot space and still works as a stove.

phrases.english: A kupach, whether lengthwise
or widthwise, is pure.
phrases.notes: It has only one pot space, so any split ruins it.

steps.whatToRemember: A כופח has one pot space and a כירה has two. The purity laws for a split stove confirm this.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוסי בר חנינא's definition with a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The definition that a כופח has one pot space and a כירה has two.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in the laws of כלים: a כירה split widthwise stays טמאה, while a כופח split any way is טהור.

steps.title: משנה: no cooking an egg with indirect heat
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה forbids placing an egg by a hot urn, roasting it in heated cloths, or burying it in sun-heated sand or road dust. רבי יוסי permits the cloths case.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not put an egg next to a hot urn so that it will roast. Nor may one roast it in cloths, but רבי יוסי permits this. Nor may one bury it in sand or road dust so that it will roast.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists ways of cooking an egg without a direct fire and says they are forbidden on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The urn's heat comes from fire, so cooking next to it is real cooking. Cloths and sand heated by the sun are not fire, but they look like cooking, so חכמים forbade them. רבי יוסי disagrees about the cloths.

keyTerms.meaning: Roast it in, or crack it into, heated cloths

steps.confusionAlert: תתגלגל does not mean 'roll' here. It means the egg gets lightly cooked from the heat.

phrases.english: MISHNAH
One may not place an egg beside the urn
so that it will roast slightly,
and one may not roast it in (sun-heated) cloths.
phrases.notes: רש"י explains this as cracking it open onto cloths heated by the sun.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei permits it.
And one may not bury it in sand or road dust
so that it will roast.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins after the earlier topic is closed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cooking an egg by the heat of an urn, in heated cloths, or in sun-heated sand or dust is forbidden on שבת. רבי יוסי permits the cloths case.

steps.title: The story of the טבריה water pipe
steps.stepSummary: The משנה tells how the people of טבריה ran a cold-water pipe through a hot spring canal.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an incident: the people of טבריה brought a pipe of cold water through a channel of hot water.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells a story. This sets up the ruling of חכמים in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people of טבריה wanted their drinking water heated on שבת without using fire. They let the hot spring water warm the cold water as it flowed through the pipe.

phrases.english: An incident that the people of Tiberias did:
they brought a pipe of cold water
through a channel of hot water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a story about another kind of indirect heating.

steps.title: The ruling of חכמים on the טבריה water
steps.stepSummary: Water heated this way on שבת is forbidden for bathing and drinking. On יום טוב it is forbidden for bathing but permitted for drinking.
steps.simpleTranslation: חכמים said to them: If it was on שבת, it is like hot water heated on שבת, and it is forbidden for bathing and for drinking. If it was on יום טוב, it is like hot water heated on יום טוב, and it is forbidden for bathing but permitted for drinking.
steps.whatsHappening: חכמים rule that this water counts as water heated on that day. On שבת it is fully forbidden, and on יום טוב it may only be drunk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת, water heated in a forbidden way cannot be used at all. On יום טוב, cooking for food and drink is allowed, so drinking is fine. Bathing is still forbidden because it is not for eating.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that heating with a non-fire source can still bring the full rules of water heated on שבת.

phrases.english: The Sages said to them:
If on Shabbat, it is like hot water heated on Shabbat,
and it is forbidden for bathing and for drinking.

phrases.aramaic: אִם בְּיוֹם טוֹב — כְּחַמִּין שֶׁהוּחַמּוּ בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: If on Yom Tov, it is like hot water heated on Yom Tov,
and it is forbidden for bathing but permitted for drinking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling on the story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Water heated this way on שבת is forbidden for bathing and drinking. On יום טוב it is forbidden for bathing and permitted for drinking.

steps.title: What if someone did roast the egg?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the law is for someone who actually roasted an egg by the urn.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: If he roasted the egg, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It asks how serious it is if someone broke the משנה's rule and roasted the egg next to the urn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only said 'one may not.' It did not say whether doing so is a Torah-level sin or only a rabbinic one.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
It was asked of them, a real open question

phrases.english: GEMARA
A question was raised before them:
If he roasted it, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the egg case in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether someone who roasted the egg by the urn is liable on a Torah level.

steps.title: רב יוסף: liable for a חטאת
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rules that someone who roasted the egg is liable to bring a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: If he roasted it, he is liable to bring a sin-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers that this is real cooking by Torah law. Someone who did it by mistake must bring a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The urn's heat comes from a fire, so cooking with it counts as true cooking, even though the egg never touched the fire. That makes it a Torah-level מלאכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Liable to bring a sin-offering, which applies to an accidental Torah-level violation

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
If he roasted it, he is liable to a sin-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is Torah-level cooking, and he is liable to bring a חטאת.

steps.title: מר בריה דרבינא begins a proof
steps.stepSummary: מר בריה דרבינא says a source supports רב יוסף. The source itself comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בריה דרבינא said: We also learned this:
steps.whatsHappening: This line introduces a proof for רב יוסף. The quote itself continues in the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The formula 'we also learned' signals that a משנה will be brought to support רב יוסף's ruling. The proof itself has not appeared yet.

phrases.english: Mar, son of Ravina, said:
We too have also learned:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבִינָא: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a supporting source for רב יוסף.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's ruling that roasting the egg makes one liable for a חטאת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה that is quoted on the next amud.
